title: fix: preserve recovery sources and readmit state after update Doctor
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor could move legacy session sources despite unavailable shared-state recovery history, and an updater could reuse stale schema admission after its Doctor child migrated the database.

## User Impact

Destructive Doctor session migrations now refuse before importing or archiving legacy sources when the shared-state database is missing but its SQLite sidecars remain. The error asks operators to restore the matching database and preserve the sidecars. After an update Doctor child settles, including a failed exit, the next parent access admits the resulting schema again and refuses unsupported newer versions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical-path optimization in #175129 removed a registry read that had incidentally blocked the unsafe migration. Put the explicit orphan-sidecar refusal in Doctor's existing target-preparation owner, before source mutations, and retain the optimization.

The warm-cache simplification in #175077 left existing parent handles usable after admission revocation. Drain the affected handles through the existing path-scoped asynchronous lifecycle owner before revoking admission and releasing process custody. No per-read schema probes, new state, or new migration machinery are introduced. Both contracts are documented.

## Evidence

On main `cec76b0b41d2`, both Doctor-child exit-code cases and the shared-state orphan-WAL case reproduced. All existing assertions remain unchanged, including exact legacy-source and WAL byte preservation. The fix passes all 11 cases in the two owning files and 65 sibling cases covering delegated authority, child settlement, recovery, and restore paths, using native Node 24 and `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`.

Core tsgo, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, both edited docs' MDX checks, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent P2 autoreview is scoped-clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The simplified change adds only the missing lifecycle close and the explicit destructive-migration admission guard: production +21/-4 lines, docs +11/-0; no tests changed.

The OAuth invalid_grant failure in the same hourly is separately covered by the active non-draft diff of #175069 and is not changed or claimed fixed here. Current-main and open-PR duplicate checks found no other fix for these two cases. No CI dispatch or rerun was requested; PR CI supplies broad proof.

### PostgreSQL failure attribution after PR CI

Job 117343061337 tested merge `bdcc9301dd58`, combining this PR with main `8324bae8896e`. That main revision contains #175157's migration of local file observation into a worker, while this PR's own base predates it. The existing PostgreSQL test's in-process filesystem mock no longer receives worker observations. Landed `90e9222398af` reconnects that fixture without weakening its product assertions.

Using the native conformance runner, Node 24, `--maxWorkers=1`, and the same pinned PostgreSQL 17/pgvector image as CI:

| Tested revision | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Current main `8c4ea360522c` | 7/7 pass |
| Unchanged PR head `0a76e07bc43d` | 7/7 pass |
| CI's main parent `8324bae8896e` | All three hosted assertion signatures reproduce; 4 failed / 3 passed overall, with the same missed insertion also affecting the result-cap case |

The historical-main comparison explicitly selected that revision's source plugin tree after an initial attempt encountered a stale local built plugin export; that initial attempt is excluded from the matching evidence. The qualified run reproduced the old cobalt snippet, old vector snippet/0.56 score, and missing boundedmarker snippet exactly. These failures are inherited and the narrow fixture repair is already on main. No source changes or branch push were needed; the existing P2 review remains applicable. No CI was dispatched or rerun.
